## Rest

- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/webhooks/): Webhooks are HTTPS posts from PayPal to an endpoint on your server whenever the corresponding event type occurs (see: [Webhook event…
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/postman): Use Postman to explore PayPal's REST APIs without a developer account. You can customize requests and receive responses for any of PayPal's core APIs.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/authentication): PayPal REST APIs use [OAuth 2.0](https://oauth.net/2/) access tokens to authenticate requests. Your access token authorizes you to use the PayPal REST API server.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/webhooks/event-names): PayPal supports these webhook events:
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/webhooks/events-dashboard/): Use the Webhooks Events dashboard to perform these tasks for your sandbox and live apps:
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/webhooks/rest/): This guide covers technical details for implementing a webhook listener and verifying messages received.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/production/): After you've tested your application in the [sandbox](https://developer.paypal.com/sandbox-testing/overview), move your application to PayPal's production environment to go live.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/info-security-guidelines/): This document provides important security related guidelines and best practices for both development projects and system integrations. The following two main topics are covered:
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/codespaces): A codespace is a cloud-based development environment. You can collaborate, build, and test code in a codespace.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/responses/): PayPal API calls return HTTP status codes.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/webhooks/simulator): You can use the simulator to post a mock webhook event message to any listener on HTTPS port 443.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/orders/v2/errors/): Errors are listed by endpoint and then by error name.
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/reference/policies-and-guidelines/): Use the following policies, guidelines, and best practices when you create applications that make calls to PayPal API operations:
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/requests/): To make a REST API request, you combine the HTTP `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE` method, the URL to the API service, the URI to a resource to query, submit data to,…
- [On this page](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/sandbox/codespaces): A codespace is a cloud-based development environment. You can collaborate, build, and test code in a codespace.
